summary: pi.dev (earendil-works/pi, MIT-licensed, formerly pi-mono / @mariozechner scope) is an actively maintained, security-conscious, minimal/extensible coding-agent harness with 84.8k GitHub stars, ~2-5 releases/week, and a first-class, officially documented fork/rebrand mechanism (package.json `piConfig`) plus a documented Claude Code skills-compat path (`~/.claude/skills` in settings.json) and CLAUDE.md already supported as a context file — meaning strape's rename and Claude-compat goals are achievable via config only, with zero source patches, which is ideal for staying mergeable with upstream. The main friction points are the strict contributor gate (new PRs auto-closed until an issue earns `lgtm`) and a documented lack of sandboxing (security is delegated to external containment), plus 4 historical CVEs (all fixed by v0.79.0, current v0.84.0).
key_facts: Official, documented, no-source-patch fork/rebrand mechanism: packages/coding-agent/docs/development.md has a "## Forking / Rebranding" section: set `"piConfig": {"name": "<yourname>", "configDir": ".<yourdir>"}` in package.json and change the `bin` field. This drives APP_NAME, APP_TITLE, CONFIG_DIR_NAME, and env var prefixes (`<NAME>_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, `<NAME>_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`) everywhere in the code (verified in packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:487-496, package.json:2-8). Source: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/development.md

extensions.md explicitly instructs extension authors: "Use CONFIG_DIR_NAME instead of hardcoding .pi ... Rebranded distributions can use a different config directory name" (packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md:953) — confirms rebranding is a first-class, intentionally supported use case. CONFIG_DIR_NAME/getAgentDir/etc. are also exported from the SDK entry point (docs/sdk.md:1175-1178) for embedders.

Setting configDir to '.claude' in piConfig would make pi look for project resources at <cwd>/.claude/{skills,prompts,themes} (resource-loader.ts join(this.cwd, CONFIG_DIR_NAME, ...)) and global agent state at ~/.claude/agent/ — nested inside the real ~/.claude dir rather than directly overwriting Claude Code's own ~/.claude/settings.json, but this co-location is a design tradeoff to weigh.

Claude Code skill reuse is already officially documented WITHOUT needing configDir tricks: packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md ('Using Skills from Other Harnesses') shows adding `"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]` (global) or `"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]` (project, in .pi/settings.json) to settings.json to load Claude Code's skill directories directly. Pi implements the open Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io) also used by Claude Code and Codex, and is deliberately lenient about directory-name vs skill-name mismatches 'for shared skill directories used across multiple agent harnesses.'

CLAUDE.md support is already built-in per the given context (resource-loader.ts candidate list: AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, AGENTS.MD, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.MD); docs/security.md states context files 'load regardless of trust status' — no patch needed to reuse existing CLAUDE.md files.

LICENSE (github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/LICENSE, verified via raw fetch) is plain MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner — no Fair Source/BSL clauses in the core repo; permissive enough for renaming/rebranding/redistributing under a new name provided the MIT notice is retained. Note: WebSearch summaries reference an 'open-core RFC 0015' business model where Earendil may license future/commercial components differently, but current repo/packages are MIT.

Repo health, verified live via GitHub REST API (api.github.com/repos/earendil-works/pi): 84,810 stars, 10,504 forks, 92 open issues, created 2025-08-09, last push 2026-08-06 (today) — very active. License field: MIT.

Release cadence, verified via api.github.com/repos/earendil-works/pi/releases: v0.84.0 published 2026-08-06T11:07:05Z, v0.83.0 on 2026-07-29, v0.82.1/v0.82.0 on 2026-07-25/24, v0.81.1/v0.81.0 both on 2026-07-21, v0.80.10/.9/.8 all between 2026-07-14 and 2026-07-16 — roughly 2-5 releases per week, sometimes multiple same-day patch releases.

CONTRIBUTING.md (raw fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) confirms: 'All issues and PRs from new contributors are auto-closed by default.' A maintainer must reply `lgtmi` (future issues not auto-closed) or `lgtm` (future issues AND PRs not auto-closed) before a PR will even be reviewed; PRs opened without prior `lgtm` are closed unread. Enforced by CI workflows present in local clone: issue-gate.yml, pr-gate.yml, approve-contributor.yml, issue-triage-labels.yml, issue-analysis.yml.

Upstreaming implication: any strape patch destined for pi core must first go through an issue (not a PR) and earn lgtm/lgtmi before a PR is accepted; CONTRIBUTING.md also states 'If your feature does not belong in the core, it should be an extension. PRs that bloat the core will likely be rejected.'

Four published GitHub Security Advisories exist for @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, all disclosed 2026-06-08 (verified via api.github.com/repos/earendil-works/pi/security-advisories, cross-checked on GitLab Advisory Database): GHSA-mqxh-6gq7-558m/CVE-2026-54325 (medium — project-local extensions loaded without approval, fixed 0.79.0), GHSA-jfgx-wxx8-mp94/CVE-2026-54328 (high — predictable temp extension install paths, local privesc, fixed 0.78.1), GHSA-7v5m-pr3q-6453/CVE-2026-54326 (low — XSS in HTML session export via Markdown URL sanitization bypass, fixed 0.78.1, reported by CrowdStrike researchers), GHSA-r95r-rj6r-c39x/CVE-2026-54327 (low — race condition in auth.json writes could transiently expose API keys/OAuth tokens, fixed 0.78.1, also CrowdStrike). Local clone version 0.84.0 postdates all four fixes.

Security model (docs/security.md, fetched from pi.dev/docs/latest/security): pi has NO built-in sandbox by design — 'Built-in tools can read files, write files, edit files, and run shell commands with the permissions of the pi process.' Docs reject partial sandboxing as false security and recommend external containment (container/VM the whole pi process, route tool exec through Gondolin micro-VMs, avoid mounting ~/.pi/agent, read-only mounts, restrict network). Prompt injection from untrusted content is explicitly out of scope for their vulnerability program.

Trust model detail (docs/security.md): project-local resources (.pi/settings.json, .pi/ extensions/skills/prompts/themes, .pi/SYSTEM.md, .agents/skills) require an explicit one-time trust decision cached in ~/.pi/agent/trust.json; non-interactive modes (-p, --mode json, --mode rpc) skip the prompt unless defaultProjectTrust: 'always' is set — audit this if strape plans headless/CI usage.

Supply-chain tooling verified in local clone: scripts/publish.mjs runs `npm publish --access public --provenance --ignore-scripts` (npm provenance attestations used for releases). .github/workflows/npm-audit.yml runs daily (cron '37 7 * * *') `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate`, and `npm audit signatures --omit=dev`, with all GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHAs.

AGENTS.md dependency-security rules (raw fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/AGENTS.md): 'Treat npm dep and lockfile changes as reviewed code. Direct external deps stay pinned to exact versions.' New deps with lifecycle scripts require explicit review/allowlisting in scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs; pre-commit blocks lockfile commits unless PI_ALLOW_LOCKFILE_CHANGE=1.

Providers doc (pi.dev/docs/latest/providers, fetched): OpenAI supported via OAuth login (ChatGPT Plus/Pro) or OPENAI_API_KEY; xAI/Grok supported via '/login xai' (subscription) or XAI_API_KEY; both are first-class built-in providers — directly matches strape's 'Grok + OpenAI only' goal. Anthropic can simply be left unconfigured/unused per the documented credential-resolution order (no code change needed to disable a provider).

SDK (pi.dev/docs/latest/sdk, packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md): @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent exports createAgentSession, createAgentSessionRuntime, ModelRuntime, DefaultResourceLoader/ResourceLoader, SettingsManager, defineTool, and run-mode helpers (InteractiveMode, runPrintMode, runRpcMode), enabling strape to embed pi as a library and customize system prompt, tools, extensions, and resource loading without forking the TUI/CLI at all.

Docs still contain stale cross-references to the pre-rename repo name 'pi-mono' (development.md: `git clone https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono`, AGENTS.md link points to .../pi-mono/...). Verified live: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-mono now returns HTTP redirect ('Moved Permanently') to earendil-works/pi — confirms canonical repo is earendil-works/pi today, with minor doc lag after the rename.

Known community forks exist and validate the piConfig rebrand path in practice (per WebSearch, not independently deep-verified): can1357/oh-my-pi, kingargyle/pi-fork, elpapi42/pi-fork, HazAT/pi-config (dotfiles repo cloned to ~/.pi/agent/). A live GitHub issue (badlogic/pi-mono#3476) shows a real downstream rebrand hit an incomplete-branding bug (a hardcoded 'Quit pi' string not using APP_NAME) — piConfig rebranding works overall but not 100% coverage everywhere; a strape rebrand should grep for remaining hardcoded 'pi'/'π' strings after setting piConfig.

pi.dev homepage/docs (fetched) reiterate the philosophy: 'Pi is a minimal agent harness. Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other way around' — no sub-agents, plan mode, MCP, or permission popups baked into core; these are meant to be added via TypeScript extensions (50+ official examples cited). This underlies why core PRs are discouraged and config/extensions (piConfig, skills paths) are the sanctioned customization surface.
risks: Setting configDir to '.claude' couples strape's global agent state directory (~/.claude/agent/, containing auth.json, trust.json, models.json, sessions) inside the same top-level folder Claude Code already owns on the user's machine. While the specific subpath likely won't collide with existing Claude Code files today, it creates a shared-namespace dependency: a future Claude Code release adding its own ~/.claude/agent/ directory, or a strape upgrade changing what it writes there, could collide. Consider only aliasing project-level skills/CLAUDE.md paths (already achievable without touching configDir) and keeping the global CONFIG_DIR_NAME strape-specific (e.g. .strape) to avoid ever writing into the user's real ~/.claude tree.

Upstream releases 2-5x per week with explicit breaking-change notes in changelogs (e.g., v0.80.7 renamed sendSessionIdHeader to sessionAffinityFormat). A strape fork/wrapper must budget recurring maintenance time to review CHANGELOG.md and re-test after each pull, especially if strape patches any source files (as opposed to using only piConfig + settings.json + SDK/extension hooks, which are far more update-resilient).

No built-in sandbox is a deliberate design choice pi's maintainers will not change; strape inherits full-filesystem/shell-command exposure at the user's privilege level unless strape adds its own containment layer (Docker/VM/Gondolin-style). Given the user's stated 'biggest concern is supply-chain/dependency security,' this needs an explicit strape-side decision since pi itself provides no sandbox.

Any source-level patch to pi core (as opposed to config/extension-based customization) will very likely never be accepted upstream without first opening an issue and getting lgtm from a maintainer — and CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly says core-bloating PRs 'will likely be rejected' even then. This makes staying on pure config/extension/SDK customization (no core diffs) the only realistically maintainable long-term strategy for the stated maintainability goal.

Four real CVEs (disclosed 2026-06-08) show the trust/extension-loading and credential-storage code has had exploitable bugs in the past (arbitrary code exec from untrusted repos, privesc via predictable temp paths, credential exposure via a permissions race). Although fixed by v0.79.0/0.78.1 and the local clone is on 0.84.0, this validates the supply-chain concern is well-founded and argues for pinning to well-audited releases and monitoring GHSA/OSV feeds for @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent and its sibling packages going forward.

The open-core business model (RFC 0015, referenced only via WebSearch summaries, not independently verified on rfc.earendil.com in this pass) suggests Earendil may introduce Fair-Source or proprietary components alongside the MIT core over time. Any future strape dependency on a non-core Earendil package should have its license explicitly checked before adoption — do not assume everything under earendil-works is MIT just because the core packages are.
recommendations: Use piConfig in a thin wrapper package.json ({"name": "strape", "bin": {"strape": "dist/cli.js"}}) as the primary rename mechanism instead of patching source strings — this is the officially documented, most-maintainable path (docs/development.md 'Forking / Rebranding' section) and keeps 100% of upstream source untouched. Follow up with a grep for residual hardcoded 'pi'/'π' UI strings post-rebrand (per the real oh-my-pi/badlogic#3476 issue) and file any gaps as extension-level overrides rather than core patches.

For Claude-compat, don't repurpose CONFIG_DIR_NAME at all initially — it's not required. Ship default settings.json with "skills": ["~/.claude/skills"] (global) and "skills": ["../.claude/skills"] (per-project, if desired) as documented in docs/skills.md, and rely on the already-built-in CLAUDE.md context-file fallback. This achieves the goal with zero forking risk and zero coupling to Claude Code's ~/.claude global directory structure.

Prefer the SDK/embedding surface (createAgentSession, ResourceLoader overrides, defineTool, custom extensionFactories) over a git fork where possible — it lets strape depend on @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent as a versioned npm dependency (easy npm update to pull upstream) rather than maintaining a diverged git fork that needs manual rebase/merge on every upstream release.

Adopt/extend pi's own supply-chain practices for the strape wrapper repo: pin all GitHub Actions to commit SHAs, run npm ci --ignore-scripts plus daily npm audit --omit=dev and npm audit signatures, and require npm publish --provenance for any strape package releases — mirroring what earendil-works/pi already does (verified in .github/workflows/npm-audit.yml and scripts/publish.mjs).

Only enable OpenAI and xAI providers by populating auth.json/env vars for those two and leaving Anthropic credentials unset — no code change is needed to restrict providers per the documented credential-resolution order; optionally use enabledModels (settings.json) to hide Anthropic model entries from /model pickers for UX cleanliness.

Given the CVE history around project-local extension trust and auth.json handling, explicitly set/document defaultProjectTrust behavior for any non-interactive/CI use of strape, and confirm strape stays pinned to >=0.79.0 (already true at 0.84.0); add @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (and sibling pi-ai/pi-agent-core/pi-tui packages) to strape's dependency-monitoring/advisory-watch list.

Treat CONTRIBUTING.md's issue-first/lgtm-gated process as a hard constraint when planning any upstream contribution: budget for opening a well-scoped issue and waiting for maintainer sign-off before writing a PR, and default to solving problems via strape-side extensions/config rather than core patches whenever the fix 'does not belong in the core' per pi's own stated philosophy.
